utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhibeqiri, did you give this interview?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You state there that you cooperated with investigators of the Tribunal. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I considered the International Crisis Group, the ICG, also as part of The Hague Tribunal. That's what I had in mind when I said that, because they said that they would take all the evidence to The Hague Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't know where this is leading, but is it not the duty of everyone to cooperate with the ICTY investigators? Is that not a universal duty?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, but the witness is providing misinformation on that matter as well. He didn't say now that he was cooperating with investigators of the Tribunal but with the International Crisis Group.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought that they were from The Hague Tribunal. It was at that time that I learned what the International Crisis Group was. Because before that we did not have anything to do with such associations. We didn't know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Haxhibeqiri. On the same page, Albanian collaborators are mentioned who were actually discussed earlier during today's testimony. You never heard of an Albanian killing an Albanian - this is page 67, line 6 - or that the KLA committed violent acts, as well as -- this is on page 65, lines 15, 16, and 17. I'm going to read the last three sentences. What -- the references that I gave are in today's transcript. [In English] "... and including the Jakupis apparently decamped with the retreating Serbian forces. Others, Haxhibeqiri said, were caught by Kosovo Liberation Army fighters." May I continue? I will continue. "And executed in apparent violation of the Geneva Convention rules governing conduct during the war." [Interpretation] Is it true that you said this for this well-known media organisation?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it could be repeated in Albanian again, please, the last lines of the questions -- of the question, sorry, including "the Serbian forces."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: The last question was whether you said that, whether you stated that. If you didn't understand what I read just now, perhaps you could say that and then we could read that again.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it possible to listen to it again, to the question again, and the citation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I will read to you what is said here.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: "The fate of those collaborators remains a mystery. Many, including the Jakupis, apparently decamped with the retreating Serbian forces. Others, Haxhibeqiri said, were caught by KLA fighters and executed in apparent violation of the Geneva Convention rules governing conduct during war." And the question is whether you told the journalist that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. These words were written by the journalist, but then I denied them and I wrote an article the next day to deny that they were my words. Those were not my words. I don't know who he talked -- who was the person he talked to. I reacted immediately the next day. It could be the day after that possibly because I couldn't sleep at night when I read the words that were written there. I was very concerned and very upset by these words that were attributed to me. I now remember very well. And if you have the article you might have my response, my rebuttal.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Why didn't you tell us that right away when we mentioned this article? And when we asked you whether you had given that interview, you said yes.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I just remembered it, this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So you just happened to remember it now?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and in fact I now remember the interview -- the interviewer and also the whole case. You asked me before and you said: Are these your words? And I said: Yes. But the last paragraph, I see that these are not my words.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: How can you see that if you can't read English?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's argumentative -- and we can hear him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Indeed. It possibly could be described in other ways as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Where did you publish a denial and when, if you did?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where the -- this article was published, the newspaper that published this in Albanian, or maybe it was translated and published in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What newspaper?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it must have been Koha Ditore or another newspaper after the war. I can't remember exactly. But I think it could be Koha Ditore.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did you keep a copy?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could you deliver a copy, if necessary?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have a copy with me now, but I can send it to the Tribunal later.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhibeqiri --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's my pleasure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- are you able to read English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not very well anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you read some English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which part are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, not in particular. I was just curious to know the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you mentioned the collaborators from among the ranks of the Albanian people, are you familiar with the name Niko Pero [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nike Peraj, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What do you know about him?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know he was an officer of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Was he a criminal like all the other Albanians serving in the Yugoslav army, police, and other institutions?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't. He wasn't known for any crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... not a criminal and all the others are?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. I think that's argumentative as well. He said some of the other Albanians who participated in the government were doing it against their will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think this statement was exclusive and referred to all the Albanians who collaborated, and I can refer you to the page number and the line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's see the line then on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Page number 39 -- or 36, 39, and the line number 5 and 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Where is the reference to criminals?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Page number 37, line 25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What would your answer be now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just hold on a second until I follow this answer. Well, that's far from a clear statement that every collaborator was a criminal. So if you want to put the question, you'll have to put it on exactly the terms in which the answer was given previously, if you really think it's worth following it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, by your leave, could the witness be shown the two lines we have just referred to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't know the answer to that. Can he be shown a part of the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: May I read it for a second, please? "They have been a part of every crime in our municipality. They have committed crimes."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Haxhibeqiri, you stated this today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I would now like to go back to health care. Do you know when the director of the health centre and the hospital were replaced? They were Albanians and they were replaced by Serbs.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not exactly the date, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What would you say if I were to tell you that almost all the positions of leadership in the hospital were held by Albanians, with the exception of Dr. Mira Antokovic and Dr. Aleksandar Antonijevic?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because you did not have the people to cover all those positions, you did not have the cadres to do that. So only the director of the hospital was known to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And what would you say if I were to give you the following names: Dr. Bozilo, Backo Bibercic, Dr. Milutin Andric, Dr. Lidija Isailovic, Dr. Nikola Jakic, Dr. Lozica Jakic --

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Dr. Olivera Micic, Dr. Jadranka Ljubenov, Dr. Marina Ljubenov. Are you familiar with those names?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, none of them. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you familiar with the name of Dr. Antonijevic?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was a lung specialist. My father was a patient of his. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to his handicapped son in June 1999?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not know him, but I know -- I knew that he was a good doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My pleasure.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the court administration open Exhibit P330? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In your statement you say that this publication entitled "the Serb genocide against the Albanian culture in Djakovica in the period the 24th of March to the 13th of June, 1999" was published. Are you aware of this publication?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Is everything contained in this report a cultural site?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, mainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Why is the damage to the Catholic church of St. James in Djakovica not mentioned here?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That church did not function. There were -- there was collateral damage done to it by the NATO air-strikes. It was the old church. That church did not have the permission to be built in the first place, and after the war they built a new church which is the highest building in Gjakova. During the war it was also mined by the Serbian forces and the NATO came later and demined the church, although it wasn't functioning as a church at all. It was damaged, yes. It's not me who organised this exhibition. It was given to me -- it was given to me by the --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... can agree --

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- investigator Clifford Smith who gave it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. But we can agree it was damaged by the NATO bombing?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you aware that another Catholic church in Djakovica was damaged, the church of St. Peter and St. Paul?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that. Who damaged them?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What would you say if I were to put the following to you? I owe the Court an apology because the following document might introduce some confusion. This was published by Mr. Andras Riedlmayer and Mr. Herscher in their investigation of the destruction of the cultural heritage in Kosovo in 1998 and 1999. The letter I'm holding in my hand is from the web site of this Tribunal. Unfortunately, in spite of a prolonged search, we managed to find only a version in B/C/S. I wish to point out that part of the work of these two well-known gentlemen -- or rather, part of the report I'm referring to is included in the documents tendered by the Prosecution in this case bearing the number P1550. On page 3 of the document I have in my hand in paragraph 2.1, damage to the cultural heritage ascribed to the NATO bombing, one can find, inter alia, the following sentence: "A Catholic church which was disused (the church of Sts. Peter and Paul in Djakovica) also suffered damage due to air-strikes and a rocket attack on a nearby Yugoslav army base." Mr. Haxhibeqiri, are you aware that some other cultural monuments were destroyed in Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me which ones?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The monumental Carshia with over 500 businesses. It was -- 90 per cent of it was burnt down. The mosque was shelled and burned. It was a mosque of the -- built in the 16th century.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... for interrupting you, but the damage you mention is mentioned in this document about Serb genocide upon Albanian culture of Gjakova --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your question, Mr. Cepic, was an open question: Are you aware that some other cultural monuments were destroyed in Djakovica? Now, did you intend to confine that to damage by NATO action?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, Your Honour. My intention was to avoid repeating what is already contained in this publication but rather to establish everything that was destroyed in Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well then, Your Honour, my objection is the question should have been: Are you aware of monuments destroyed other than those listed in the document entitled "Serb genocide upon Albanian culture"? As you indicated, this is an open question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Well, rephrase the question then, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhibeqiri, would you tell me what other cultural monuments were destroyed in Djakovica, apart from the ones listed in the agenda we have just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, perhaps it might be helpful to give the witness a copy of the document because he may not be able to have in his head all those that are listed in the document. I have a hard copy I could hand him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is there some -- is there some reason why you want the witness to do this from memory?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Carry on on that basis then.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The well-known towers, stone towers, in the villages of Gjakova, historical monuments, centuries old --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Can the witness tell us what page he's referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: My specific question: Is this a cultural monument?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. This is the tower in the old Carshia.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Page 2 and page 3, the page number is underneath the picture. This is the old town, page 4. And then on page 6 is the Hadum mosque. Do you know how the old town was damaged, the Carshia, which we saw in the previous pictures?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Describe this.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am a witness -- eye-witness of the destruction of this mosque when the shells of the Yugoslavian army destroyed this object. I've seen the moment when it fell down, when it collapsed, because at that time I was facing the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And at that point in time you observed the bomb exploding and blowing up the mosque and you were outside in the street?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard the explosion, and there was this great cloud of dust. I couldn't see anything else. I saw that the minaret collapsed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Where were you at that point?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At home.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So how were you able to see this?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you see the mosque from your flat?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the place where I was, in my yard, 50 yards away as the crow flies you can see the mosque from there. It's even closer than that, maybe even closer than 50 yards. Because all the shops around the place where I live, they were all burnt down. So it was possible for me to see the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What time of day was it?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was reading a book and some pieces of rocks and stone and debris fell on my book, and this happened at 1308 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So we can conclude that you did not see this directly, that you only heard the explosion and saw the fragments that flew into your room. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The debris fell on my book, yes, and I heard the explosion. And later I saw that the minaret was cut in half.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: When was this approximately, what date?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it once. Maybe I should repeat it again? It was during the time when there was fighting in the Kodra e Cabratit. I think it was the 8th of May. I'm referring to the fightings from the 7th to the 11th of May. I think it was the 8th of May, and the hour, I'm sure it was 1.00 p.m., 1.08 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: On the basis of what do you conclude that it was a JNA bomb that destroyed the minaret?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say "a bomb." Who else?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that the only answer you want to give to that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you addressing me, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, it's an entirely unsatisfactory answer to say "who else." You're invited to say positively why you concluded it was a JNA attack that caused the damage to the minaret.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But there were witnesses who saw the other object, the obelisk of the league of Prizren, which is a hundred metres from my house. And it collapsed after two or three attempts that they made at shelling it. The forces were seen placing the mines to this object.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... mosque?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was almost on the same day, the same day that the explosion happened also in the house of Tafa of Ali Aga, which is also a monument of culture. It was under the protection of the state.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhibeqiri, you keep avoiding to be giving an answer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, you carry on as if you're pursuing -- no, no, please, if you're pursuing it. I was going to pursue it if you were not. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This photograph here, this is the photograph I am talking about, K0386286. This is the old house, which is a monument of culture under protection of the state. It happened on the same day that it was burnt down, the whole of it, the whole house. It's oriental-style house.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you allow me, I'm afraid that the witness all time has been avoiding -- avoiding to answer on my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're abandoning this -- the question, are you? Mr. Haxhibeqiri, you're being asked on what basis you concluded that the JNA, as you call them, were responsible for destroying this minaret. Now, what is it you saw that led to -- or heard that led you to that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard the explosion and I saw the situation, what it was like, after the explosion. During that time it was only these forces that operated in the area, during those four days. They burned over a hundred houses and cultural monuments. The citizens saw them burning these objects, this house -- these houses, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So are you saying that it was -- well, we're still talking about the mosque at the moment. Now, how is it you say the mosque was destroyed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was an offensive of these forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, but how did they do it? We've had three possible versions so far. We've had shelling, we've had burning, and we've had mining. Now, what is it that you say was done to the mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The obelisk of the league of Prizren, I said that it was mined; the mosque was shelled; while the house that I mentioned, it was burned. The mosque was also burned on the first night, the internal part of it. On the 25th of March, it was burned inside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, you said earlier and you've said now that the mosque was shelled. What was it that you saw or heard that led you to the conclusion that it was shelled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that I heard a huge explosion and I didn't see anyone there after the explosion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Well, that's as far as I can take it, Mr. Cepic. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd be grateful if we could show the map of Djakovica to the witness. It is P10.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhibeqiri, do you have that map in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Do you need a hard copy for you to be able to show us where you were at that moment?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Carshia e Madhe.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us the exact address where your apartment was?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The street name is Vellezerit Frasheri, which is the Frasheri brothers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Sabbah, does this now need to -- does something here require another exhibit number? Is that -- is it because of the red mark that's the ... Mr. Cepic, do you wish the marked copy to be recorded with an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't decide on that yet, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Well, just remember to do so if you think it appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhibeqiri, would you be so kind as to point out on the map where the mosque was?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately here. I said aerial distance is no more than 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have this marked on the map with a number 1, we should mark the place where Mr. Haxhibeqiri lives, and we should use the number 2 to mark the spot where the mosque is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]. [Interpretation] South to my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but I don't seem to be able to see it clearly. I can see the little X there and something that is probably the number 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's a 1 and a 2 as you asked him to mark it. And because they're so close to each other, it's difficult to do anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And he made the point, which I think is clear from this map, that the mosque is south of his home address.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Between the mosque and your house, are there any buildings?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Two rows of shops which were totally burned.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What other buildings are there, apart from the two rows of shops?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No others, only the shops. In that direction there are only shops.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My pleasure.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: To go back to the old town, to Carshia itself, when I asked you about that you started mentioning the mosque. In your knowledge, when were the shops in the old town set ablaze?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The majority was burned on the 24th of March, the same night when the city was bombed by the NATO forces. In fact, when the NATO offensive against -- against the Serbian military targets started. As Serb reaction to the NATO attacks, the Serbs burned the old Carshia. About 200 shops were burned. I'm repeating these things over and over again.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... Your Honours. Your Honours, I would like to move on to a different topic and to go back to the issue of religious buildings at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If you really must, but you should be paying some attention to the time that's being used on what appear to be rather minor events in a much bigger picture that we have to be concerned about.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I understood Your Honour. I think that -- I think that this issue is very, very important.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Haxhibeqiri, at page 6 in the B/C/S of the transcript you stated that you conducted an investigation as to how Kujtim Dula, Izet Hima, Sadik Zherka, Qamil Zherka and Nexhmedin Zherka were killed. Mark Malota's murder was also discussed here. This is what you stated in your statement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kujtim Dula is the husband of an actress of the national theatre and I took the testimony from his wife. Her husband was killed that night. He was the first victim on the 25th of March. He was killed at -- he was killed at half past 1.00 on the 25th of March. Half an hour later, Izet Hima was killed. He was the head surgeon of the Gjakova hospital. He was massacred. Both of them, the names I mentioned, they were massacred. And further down the road two elderly people of the Zherka family were killed as well as the son of one of those two. When it dawned the following day, they were found killed in their own homes. Everyone has testified that there were police and paramilitary forces as well as local Serbs in uniform -- in police uniforms that were involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did you see that personally?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What do you mean by -- when you say that the local Serbs were in uniform, you mean in local police uniforms? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. They were wearing official police uniform -- uniforms. They were all mobilised. The adults, all Serb adults, were mobilised, almost all.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I continue the questions? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your statement you said that once you returned from the neighbourhood of Novi Blok and when you returned to your house you spent the rest of the time inside your house. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You spoke before this Tribunal about the expulsion of a great number of Albanians from Djakovica, hence my question: How come so many people were expelled, whereas you yourself were not found in your own house?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not only me who remained in Gjakova.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: How do you explain the fact that you could sit inside or in front of your house reading while the rest of Djakovica is being expelled? You were the only one to remain.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that misstates his prior testimony. He's never said he was the only one to remain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Not only that, but he's given a figure for the number who did remain.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Why did you state then that you were looked for by the police and you had to hide in the manhole?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say that the police was searching for me. And the expulsion did not take place on that date in May. So the expulsions were sporadic up until the 11th of May, and after -- after the 13th of May there were no expulsions, major expulsions. They were sporadic. I said I was hiding. I didn't say I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: How do you explain the fact that you were hiding in someone else's house and at the same time you could spend your time freely in your own house?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't stay there freely. I was following every second of how the situation was developing around myself. I did not sleep for a single night at home. I was alert at every time of the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Why did you state then that you spent all your time in the house? I can refer you to that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the time I spent at home or in the ambulance clinic courtyard, which is near my house. I was hiding behind a pine tree, the foot of that tree. That's -- that's where I was staying, and I have slept in the open for 40 days running under that tree.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Haxhibeqiri, you stated -- in the English this is page 7, paragraph 2; in the B/C/S, it is paragraph 6. There you state: "Four days later I returned to my own house, where I stayed until the war was over."

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was four days after I came out of that manhole, then I returned to my home. And during that period, I went to my -- to my uncle's for 10, 12 days because it was calmer there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Why did you state then that you were in the house all the time?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said earlier Mr. -- when Mr. Lukic asked that I have spent 10 to 12 days at my uncle's.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You didn't mention that in the statement given to the investigators?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour, but it seems I'm running out of time today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry. You've still got two minutes that you can make use of. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'll be brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In several places you mentioned the activities of the military. What basis do you have to make those conclusions?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actions of the army, we've seen them for a long time marching through the streets of the city, during the day, in the evening, or in the villages around. For a year -- for a whole year we've seen them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through the city, in the middle of the city. The column of the Yugoslav forces with tanks and the heavy artillery part of the Yugoslav army. Every day they went to the villages. They killed citizens, Albanian civilians, and burned villages. In the evening they returned as winners, victorious, and you thought it was Texas. It was -- they were partying. All paramilitary forces, policemen, soldiers, they were drunk, celebrating for the victory that they had reached over the unprotected Albanian citizens.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: How is it you know all that?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: FUAT HAXHIBEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: All that I've said I've seen them. And I'm talking about when they returned to the city. These scenes that I've described I've seen with my own eyes. They were drunk, they were pushing people around. As for the results of the burnings and the victims that they caused, it was the members of the human rights centre who were reporting to us. So our data, our evidence, has come straight for word from the scenes of the crime. Over all the data and evidence that we've put forward, nothing has been rejected or denied by the international independent investigators.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if that were the end of the two minutes, I wanted to take 30 seconds to renew my previous request that the Court consider setting some kind of limitations on cross-examination. This plays real havoc with our attempts to schedule witnesses. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, but what I would like you to do is discuss among yourselves as counsel the length of time that's going to be taken and make appropriate arrangements. I don't think the Trial Chamber should be directly involved in this, if that can be avoided. I'm beginning to consider that it may not be possible to avoid it, but meanwhile I'm leaving it to counsel to try to organise their affairs and bring matters within reason. I don't think today's a good example of that, however.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have inquired with counsel before we started this last session to see whether or not I should keep the witnesses around for -- coming on before we ended, and I was told there was a possibility. We still have four accused to go, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I'm very surprised that you were given that indication. I had assumed that in view of the personal position of the next witness that more satisfactory arrangements would have been made. However, we can now adjourn until tomorrow morning. Mr. Haxhibeqiri, you have to come back again tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning. And again I remind you, as I'm obliged to do, that you must not discuss your evidence, either what you've given or the evidence that you may give, with any person between now and resuming tomorrow at 9.00. Court is now adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 9th day of August, 2006, at 9.00 a.m.
